forecasts.reason: Lookahead averaging should absorb the LR-floor change (E009). But the detach now happens at 9% of peak LR with a live Muon momentum buffer, which is a small abrupt-freeze penalty that roughly cancels the slower-decay gain. Expect ±0.1 pp, which is below 60-draw power.
E055's slope is steep below 75%, but the learning-finished account says the curve flattens above 75%. I expect +0.05 to +0.1 pp, about break-even with the dial, so it will not clear the ≥0.12 pp bar.

Filters are renormalized every step, so the lr sets the angular step size. That is likely somewhat under-tuned for 225 steps, but the gain is probably ~0.05–0.1 pp, too small to reach 0.12 pp on 60 draws.

E062 saved 0.28 s against ~0.18 s of NS GPU time. The three reduce-overhead cudagraph Muon calls, plus the Python LR loop and write-back copies, are host-bound overhead. Merging them should recover ~0.05–0.12 s. The math is near-identical, so per-seed results only re-draw.

At batch 2000 with Lookahead resets every 5 steps, extra momentum mostly adds lag. NS normalization removes its magnitude benefit, so it should lean slightly harmful, but probably not by the ≥0.12 pp needed to refute.

This is a diagnostic with no recipe change. With LS 0.3, 225 steps and 100 classes, I expect clean train top-1 on the averaged weights of ~85–90%, which is under-fitting, and the fast weights a little lower.

cruxes: What share of each step's wall time is host overhead (the Python LR loop over 9 groups, 3 separate reduce-overhead Muon cudagraph replays, and write-back memcpys) versus GPU kernel time? If it is ≥5%, merging the optimizer (I107) is the largest zero-accuracy lever left and also shrinks the PCIe/host penalty on the judge.

Is the freeze cost an anneal-shape effect (the group-1 LR decay compressed over 23–75%) or lost late steps? I104 versus I105 splits this. If it is the anneal shape, the cheap move is to decouple anneal from detach everywhere, including group 2, rather than buy steps.

Does the averaged model under-fit (clean train top-1 ≤90%, I109)? If so, regularizers are dead, and the only remaining accuracy routes are per-step quality (Muon lr/momentum, batch) and capacity priced at the dial.
structured_output.world_model:
W5 (contrarian), after E063 crashed. The tip is still E061 at 5.02 s / 0.7534. Seeds 0–2 sit on the bar, so a recipe whose population mean is about 0.7535 passes about half the time.

1. Time is driven by step count plus per-step host and launch overhead more than by pixels. E062 saved 0.28 s by removing 3 Muon reduce-overhead graph calls per step. E061 saved about 12 ms per 20 px step. The untested lever is merging the 3 Muon instances and putting the LR tables on the GPU (I107), worth about 0.05–0.12 s at zero accuracy cost.

2. Accuracy is carried by per-step update quality on layers that are still learning. Muon is load-bearing. The freezes at 6% (whitening bias), 75% (stem) and 90% (group 2) sit at the edge of their learning curves, and earlier freezes cost.

3. A mechanism the others have not proposed: the freeze cost may come partly from the abrupt loss of the Muon momentum buffer and from Lookahead pulling the frozen stem toward stale averages. If so, it is the anneal shape, not the lost steps, that is priced. I104 versus I105 tests this.

4. Scalar retunes (Muon lr, momentum, LS) are likely within ±0.1 pp, which is below the power of 60-draw judging.

5. The recipe likely under-fits CIFAR-100, at about 85–90% clean train accuracy.
